{{Short description|American statistician and engineer}}
{{use mdy dates|date=November 2025}}
{{use list-defined references|date=November 2025}}

'''John Stuart Hunter''' (born June 3, 1923{{r|DeVeaux2020}}) is an American statistician and engineer whose career has spanned academia and industry. He is considered a pioneer of the application of statistical methods, especially [[Design of experiments|experimental design]] and [[quality control]], to [[industrial engineering]]. He is an elected fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]], the [[American Society for Quality]], and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].

==Education==
Hunter earned his BSc (1947) in [[electrical engineering]], his MS (1949) in [[engineering mathematics]], and his PhD (1954) in [[statistics]] from [[North Carolina State University]].{{r|AmStatNews2015}} His PhD thesis, ''Multi-factor experimental designs'', was written under the tutelage of Robert John Hader.{{r|MathGenealogy}}

==Career==
During [[World War II]], Hunter was [[Conscription|called up]] and joined the [[United States Army]]. He was initially assigned to the [[Army Specialized Training Program]] at NC State and later served in [[Philippines]].{{r|DeVeaux2020}} After earning his PhD he worked at [[American Cyanamid]]. He joined [[Princeton University]] in 1961, where he is now professor [[emeritus]], School of Engineering and Applied Science.{{r|DeVeaux2020}}

Hunter was the founding editor of the statistical journal [[Technometrics]] from 1959 to 1963.{{sfn|Hunter|1983}} He was [[List of presidents of the American Statistical Association|president of the American Statistical Association]] in 1992.{{r|UDaily}}

== Honors and awards ==
[[File:John_Stuart_Hunter_Wilks_Award_Letter_1987.jpg|thumb|right|In 1987, Hunter was awarded the US Army's Wilks Memorial Medal and Award]]
Hunter has been widely recognized for his contributions to statistical methodology and industrial engineering.
* 1959 and 1985, recipient of the ASQ's Brumbaugh Award{{r|ASQBrumbaugh}}
* 1961, elected [[List of fellows of the American Statistical Association|fellow of the American Statistical Association]]{{r|ASAFellows}}
* 1965, elected fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science{{r|AAAS}}
* 1970, recipient of the [[Shewhart Medal]]{{r|ASQShewhart}} 
* 1985, recipient of the ASQ's Deming Medal{{r|ASQDeming}}
* 1987, recipient of the United States Army Samuel S. Wilks Memorial Medal and Award{{r|CASD}}
* 1995, recipient of the [[American Statistical Association Founders Award]]{{r|ASAFoundersAward}}
* 1998, elected honorary member of the [[American Society for Quality]] (ASQ){{r|ASQ}}
* 2004, named Distinguished Alumnus for the College of Physical and Mathematical Sciences, North Carolina State University{{r|NCState}}
* 2005, elected member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]]{{r|NAE}}
* 2006, awarded an [[Honorary degree|honorary]] DSc from North Carolina State University{{r|UDaily}}
* 2008, awarded an honorary DSc from [[Pennsylvania State University]]{{r|UDaily}}
* 2015, recipient of the [[William Hunter (statistician)|William G. Hunter Award]] presented by the Statistics Division of the American Society for Quality{{r|WGHAward}}{{efn|William G. Hunter and John Stuart Hunter are not related.{{r|WGHAward}}}}
